design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomized using centrally generated computer random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated random sequence was centralized and allocation was revealed to the surgeon just before the procedure, with well-balanced baseline characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Simple randomization was performed centrally using computer-generated random numbers. Randomization was revealed to the operating surgeon just before starting each procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of surgical interventions was not feasible, all assigned patients received the allocated intervention and were analyzed according to an intention-to-treat approach without evidence of important deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients and authors assessing the outcomes were not blinded to the procedure. ... All the patients were included in the ﬁnal analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was zero loss to follow-up, and complete outcome data were available for all randomized patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There were 35 patients in each group. All the patients were included in the ﬁnal analysis. ... Lost to follow-up (n = 0)

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were explicitly unblinded to the treatment group, and subjective/semi-subjective outcomes including radiological reading and patient-reported pain scores could be influenced by knowledge of intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients and authors assessing the outcomes were not blinded to the procedure. ... Stone clearance was assessed using ultrasonography and X-ray plain abdominal ﬁlm of kidney,ureter and bladder at 3 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan to ensure reported outcomes and analyses were not selected post hoc.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary objective was to compare stone clearance rates and secondary objectives were to compare operating time, requirement for intra-operative JJ stenting, complications according to the Clavien–Dindo classiﬁcation system...

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to lack of outcome assessor blinding for subjective/semi-subjective outcomes and the absence of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio stratified by center using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed via central allocation until surgical scheduling, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Parallel randomization was conducted at a ratio of 1:1, stratified by site and was carried out using computer-generated random numbers. The coordinating center revealed randomization to the operating surgeon at the time of surgical scheduling.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although unblinded due to the surgical nature of the interventions, surgical protocols were standardized and the primary analyses were conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle with all randomized participants included.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The surgeons and patients were no blinded to group assignment... The analysis was done according to the intention-to-treat principle. We also did a per-protocol analysis of the primary endpoints in which we compared patients who underwent the assigned RIRS... with those who had been randomly assigned to and underwent SMP.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary and secondary endpoints were complete for all 160 randomized participants with zero loss to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Lost to follow-up (n = 0) Discontinued intervention (n = 0) Underwent randomization (n = 160) ... Intention-to-treat analysis (n = 80 [each group])

domain_judgments.rationale: Postoperative clinical assessments and imaging interpretations were conducted by blinded investigators, and objective imaging criteria (CT/ultrasound/KUB) were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Investigators who had not been involved and blinded to the surgical procedures performed the postoperative clinical assessment. Stone-free status was defined as no residual fragments of ≥0.3 cm on KUB and ultrasound at 1-day and on CT scan at 3-months after operation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov and reported all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes analyzed according to a prespecified plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered at http://clinicaltrials.gov/ (NCT02519634)... The primary endpoint was stone-free rate (SFR)... Secondary endpoints included blood loss, operating time, postoperative pain scores, auxiliary procedures, complications and hospital stay. Analysis was by intention-to-treat.

overall_summary: The trial used rigorous computer-generated central randomization, had complete follow-up of all randomized patients, blinded outcome assessors, and reported prespecified outcomes consistent with trial registration, resulting in a low risk of bias overall.

design_rationale: The authors state that 'Randomization for UMPNL or RIRS procedures was done with tossing a coin method', indicating an explicit random allocation mechanism.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation concealment was not described and coin tossing is easily subverted; moreover, there is an unexplained group imbalance (30 vs 43) and significant baseline imbalance in stone location (p=0.020).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomized into groups with tossing a coin method... Randomization for UMPNL or RIRS procedures was done with tossing a coin method, and one surgeon performed UMPNL, and another performed RIRS.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of patients and surgeons was not possible due to surgical nature, each technique was performed by a single distinct surgeon, and no trial protocol or specific analysis plan (ITT details) was provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: one surgeon performed UMPNL, and another performed RIRS. Both are highly experienced surgeons.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear to be reported for all 73 randomized patients across the primary outcomes with no evident post-randomization attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 73 patients with stone sizes of 10-25 mm, and had RIRS or UMPNL procedures were included in the study... There were 30 patients in Group I, and 43 patients in Group II.

domain_judgments.rationale: While stone-free status was assessed via CT, subjective outcomes such as pain (VAS) and time to return to normal activities were assessed in unblinded patients by an unblinded physician without blinding of outcome assessors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Postoperative pain was determined by visual analog scale (VAS), asked by the same physician to all patients 2 hours after surgery. Return to normal daily life was determined by asking the patients the time between discharge from hospital and return to work. Stone-free status was determined with low-dose non-contrast CT obtained one month after surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective clinical trial registration or pre-published statistical analysis plan was cited, leaving potential for selective reporting of outcomes and subgroup analyses (such as by stone location).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After approval of the study protocol by local ethics committee, the patients admitted to our clinic and diagnosed with renal stones and scheduled for surgery between March and September 2015 were prospectively analyzed.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial concerns regarding the randomization and allocation concealment process (coin toss without concealment leading to significant baseline imbalances and unequal group sizes), alongside the lack of blinding for subjective outcomes and absence of a pre-registered trial protocol.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either FURL or MPCNL using computer software (STATA version 13.0) to generate random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a computer-generated random sequence was generated, the study does not report allocation concealment methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Simple random sampling was adopted, and parallel randomization was conducted at a ratio of 1:1, stratified by site, and was carried out using computer software STATA /C210 version 13.0 (StataCorp LP, College Station, TX) to generate random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was unblinded and four patients in the MPCNL group had their procedure aborted and were excluded from post-procedure efficacy and pain analyses (n=106 vs n=110), representing a per-protocol rather than intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A prospective, simple random sampling and unblinded controlled study were performed... Four patients assigned in the MPCNL group had purulent fluid in the initial puncture, and the following MPCNL procedure was aborted.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 216 of 220 randomized participants (>98%), and the 4 exclusions in the MPCNL group were fully accounted for due to intraoperative findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Four patients assigned in the MPCNL group had purulent fluid in the initial puncture, and the following MPCNL procedure was aborted.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and outcome assessors were aware of the surgical intervention in an unblinded trial, which could plausibly influence subjective patient-reported outcomes such as pain (VAS) and comfort (BCS).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The severity of pain was assessed at 6, 24, and 48 hours postoperation with a visual analog scale (VAS; range: 1–10) and Bruggrmann Comfort Scale (BCS) score (ranging between 0 'persistent pain' and 4 'cough is painless').

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial pre-registration or published protocol is cited to confirm that all planned analyses and outcome measurements were reported without selection.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The stone-free rate, comfort and pain indicated by Bruggrmann Comfort Scale (BCS) and visual analog scale (VAS) were evaluated and recorded.

overall_summary: The study has some concerns regarding risk of bias overall due to lack of reported allocation concealment, unblinded assessment of subjective patient-reported outcomes (pain and comfort scores), and absence of a pre-registered trial protocol.

design_rationale: The study is a prospective randomized controlled trial in which 70 patients were randomized 1:1 to either mini-PCNL or RIRS by the Department of Biostatistics.

domain_judgments.rationale: While the sequence was generated by biostatistics and revealed on admission, there was an 'allocation error' where two patients assigned to RIRS received mini-PCNL and were dropped, and significant baseline imbalances emerged (hydronephrosis P=0.004, S-ReSC score P=0.015).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was carried out by the Department of Biostatistics of our institution and opened to the operating surgeon at the time of the patient’s admission on the day before surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was not feasible given the surgical nature, and two participants assigned to RIRS received the alternative intervention due to allocation error and were excluded rather than analyzed in an intention-to-treat framework.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two patients from the RIRS group received mini-PCNL because of the allocation error and dropped out of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 68 of 70 patients (97.1%), with only 2 dropouts due to allocation error, making it unlikely that missing data significantly biased the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 70 randomized patients, 68 completed the study including mini-PCNL in 35 and RIRS in 33. Two patients from the RIRS group received mini-PCNL because of the allocation error and dropped out of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary endpoint (stone-free status) was objectively assessed by non-enhanced computed tomography (NECT) using standardized radiological criteria.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Stone-free status was defined as no residual stones or stones <2 mm on NECT within 3 months postoperatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02067221) and the reported outcomes match the planned primary and secondary endpoints.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This prospective randomized controlled trial (NCT02067221) aimed to compare mini-PCNL and RIRS for renal stones >10 mm.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as 'some concerns' due to issues with the allocation implementation (two allocation errors with post-randomization exclusion) and notable baseline imbalances between the study groups in stone complexity and hydronephrosis.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly state that participants were randomized into either the RIRS group or the PNL group in a 1:1 ratio using an online research randomizer.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although an online randomizer was used, allocation concealment is not described, and there are baseline imbalances between groups in stone size and number of stones (p < 0.001).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After receiving patients' written informed consent, the patients were randomized into either the RIRS group (Group 1) or PNL group (Group 2) in a ratio of 1:1 by using an online research randomizer (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the surgical procedures, blinding was not feasible, but standardized postoperative care and analgesic protocols were delivered and all randomized patients appear to have received their allocated intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All patients who underwent renal stone surgery were treated with intravenous dexketoprofen trometamol, 50 mg twice daily, for the purpose of postoperative analgesic and anti-inﬂammatory treatment. Intravenous tramadol hydrochloride, 100 mg, was added to the treatment for patients who did not have their pain resolved after the initial treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Complete outcome data were available and analyzed for all 50 patients per group included in the analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: RIRS (n = 50) PNL (n = 50)

domain_judgments.rationale: Postoperative pain was measured via a patient-reported VAS questionnaire without blinding of patients to surgical intervention type (RIRS vs. percutaneous nephrostomy), which could have influenced pain reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients who were included in the study were asked to ﬁll out a visual analog scale (VAS) questionnaire at 8 and 24 hours postoperatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT02430168) and reported outcomes (postoperative VAS pain and analgesic requirement) in accordance with the pre-specified study aims.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The national clinical trial number of our study is NCT02430168 and Institutional Review Board number is IRB18-14.

design_rationale: The study explicitly describes a prospective randomized clinical trial where patients were randomized 1:1 using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although computer-generated random numbers were used, the method of allocation concealment is not explicitly detailed beyond being opened to the surgeon before surgery, raising some concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All enrolled patients were randomized to mPNL group and RIRS group with allocation 1:1. The randomization was carried out using computer-generated random numbers and opened to the operating surgeon before surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of surgical procedures blinding of surgeons and patients was not feasible, but standard protocols were adhered to without evidence of deviations from the intended interventions that would bias outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eventually, 5 patients withdrew during the treatment and follow-up phase, with 115 patients enrolled in the primary outcome analysis (58 in the mPNL group and 57 in the RIRS group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for over 95% of randomized participants (115/120) with low and balanced attrition across groups (2 in mPNL, 3 in RIRS).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among the 120 eligible patients, 60 were randomized to the mPNL group and 60 to the RIRS group. Eventually, 5 patients withdrew during the treatment and follow-up phase, with 115 patients enrolled in the primary outcome analysis (58 in the mPNL group and 57 in the RIRS group).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of stone-free status was objectively evaluated by non-contrast CT at 3 months postoperatively by assessors blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The postoperative assessment was performed by investigators who were unaware of the patients’ group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the reported primary and secondary outcomes correspond with pre-specified measures without indications of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Besides, this study was prospectively registered at http://www.chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR1800016983).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to potential limitations in the concealment of the allocation sequence prior to surgery in Domain 1, despite low risk across all other domains.
